_comment: v1.11.4 - the third De Bello Gallico batch: Book V (7) and the last two of Book VI, which closes at its allocated 6. Every excerpt is a whole chapter, so no `range` is needed and no citation names its subsections. Two source defects to watch: `apud in servitute` for `apud se in servitute` at V.27, and `contra potentio rem` for `contra potentiorem` at VI.11 - both emended. V.14 prints `Vxores` with the Latin Library's capital V for U, which is an orthographic convention and not an error, so it stays verbatim and is explained in the analysis.
bg.5.7: Qua re cognita Caesar, quod tantum civitati Aeduae
at equites Aedui ad Caesarem omnes revertuntur.
bg.5.14: Ex his omnibus longe sunt humanissimi
quo primum virgo quaeque deducta est.
bg.5.30: Hac in utramque partem disputatione habita
bg.5.37: Sabinus quos in praesentia tribunos militum
eum de rebus gestis certiorem faciunt.
bg.5.44: Erant in ea legione fortissimi viri
bg.6.11: Quoniam ad hunc locum perventum est
omnes civitates in partes divisae sunt duas.
bg.6.28: Tertium est genus eorum, qui uri appellantur
in amplissimis epulis pro poculis utuntur.
